messages:
anya: Heads-up — after the kernel-autoswitch change we rolled yesterday I'm seeing sustained all-reduce latency growth on 8xTPx4 micro-batches (32 GPUs). Not huge but reproducible: +18-35% p95 for step time.

mike: can you paste the perf snippet / nccl logs?

anya: pasted below, ran nccl-tests with the app profile and a short training trace. Notice the jump when msgsize distribution shifts to many small fragments.

anya: ```
# simplified from nsys timeline + nccl-tests rtt:
msg_size  ring_us  tree_us  count
1KB       42.1     28.3     1200
8KB       56.8     34.2     400
64KB      95.2     68.7     80
512KB     220.4    210.1    10

kernel_selector.log: selected=ring_allreduce for msgsize=8KB (heuristic: prefer ring for <64KB)
trace: many small KV cache flushes produce 1000s of 1-8KB reduce ops per step
```

rafael: interesting — our previous heuristics assumed msg_count low but now packing change means high cardinality of small reduces. Ring is cheaper for large counts but very bad for high fan-in many tiny messages due to latency per-hop. Tree wins for small msgs because of lower hop depth.

sophie: timeline shows that compute->comm overlap is close to zero for these steps. GPU stream shows comm kernels are launched serially after compute finishes. I think two things combined: (1) kernel selector picks ring so NCCL launches a lot of small ops; (2) runtime waits for full KV flush before letting non-blocking comm start, so we lost overlap.

anya: repro steps I used:
1) run training with TP config: tensor_parallel=8, micro_batch=4, kv_cache_enabled=true, kv_pack_threshold=0 (current default)
2) enable 'runtime:trace_kernelselect=true' and collect nsys
3) run: `./build/nccl-tests/all_reduce -b 1024 -e 524288 -f 2 -g 8` to get same distribution

mike: thanks. Can you attach the nsys timeline link or upload the trace?

anya: uploaded to perf dash: https://perf.redwood/internal/trace/3349994321 (private). Key excerpt: compute kernels end at t=1.234s, first comm op starts at t=1.238s but many comm launches are serialized until t=1.260s. No overlap.

rafael: quick theory: our kernel selection rule 'prefer ring for <64KB' was tuned for single large reduce per step (old shaping). But with kvcache packing disabled we hit many small reduces; ring's per-hop overhead accumulates and also NCCL launch path has higher CPU-side syncs for small ops. Tree with fanout reduces latency and gives better chance for overlap because fewer sequential launches.

sophie: also saw kernel_autoswitch path runs a synchronous check on the eager path: `query_comm_capabilities()` which stalls the runtime thread for ~200us at every batch boundary when many reduces present. That's enough to destroy compute overlap for micro-batch=4.

mike: proposed mitigations:
- revert the <64KB ring preference to a dynamic threshold: if step reduces_count > N -> switch to tree for <X KB.
- make `query_comm_capabilities()` async / cached per-step-window to avoid repeated syncs.
- re-enable aggressive kv_pack_threshold=16KB for TP runs to reduce small-frag counts.

anya: I can prototype two quick patches: tweak threshold and add a simple per-worker cache for `query_comm_capabilities()` (ttl 1s). Which one should be first?

rafael: threshold change is lowest risk. If we detect many small messages, pick tree. We should test with these three configs: (A) current, (B) threshold-change, (C) threshold + kv_pack. Run perf harness for 50 steps each and measure step p95 and overlap metric (compute_end -> comm_start).

infra-bot: deploy job queued: job/3349994321-tp-allreduce-repro (env: staging, 32gpus)

anya: created a short PR draft with the threshold gating and a small unit test for selector. PR: https://git.redwood/infer/runtime/pulls/2891 (draft). Running perf sweeps now.

mike: nice. Add a flag `--force-tree` so QA can run quick A/B without code change. Also capture nccl debug envs: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE=0` to make timeline clearer.

sophie: long term we should consider: (1) autoswitch learns from streaming metrics (histogram of msg sizes per-step) and adapts thresholds; (2) avoid any blocking capability check on-step boundary.

rafael: agreed. For now do threshold + short cache. If that fixes overlap and reduces p95 to baseline we can ship a patch. If not, we look at adding non-blocking nvlink probes and deeper NCCL tuning.

anya: results from first 3 runs (A/B/C):
A (current): p95 step +32%, avg overlap 0ms
B (threshold-change): p95 +8%, avg overlap 6ms
C (threshold + kv_pack=16KB): p95 -1% (baseline), avg overlap 12ms

anya: conclusion: short-term fix = revert packing default to 16KB for TP workloads + threshold change for selector. I'll open an ops config PR and follow up with runtime patch to make selector dynamic.

mike: sounds good. Assigning owners: anya -> runtime patch & perf runs, rafael -> selector review, sophie -> doc/ops flag. We'll merge config rollback today. :thumbsup:

anya: will post a short postmortem in #eng-runtime once it's in staging and we validate. Thanks all.
